items.reason: Needs network: resolving 40 tags to commit SHAs requires the GitHub API, and the repo already ships the one-pass closer (`npm run actions:pin`, which rewrites the workflows AND flips STRICT/RATCHET); the broad-write half the item names was already split into three single-capability jobs in issue-dispatch.yml, so I recorded the pin's direction in the contract ledger and made `actions:pin` print the ledger line it now owes instead.

Every ratchet baseline and gate threshold in the repository is now pinned in .github/contract-ledger.json with a `ceiling` or a `floor`, and `contract:ledger:check` (blocking inside check:ci, run by .husky/pre-push before the push that ships master) fails when a number crosses its pin or when a new baseline/threshold arrives unpinned.

`npm run flake:drill` runs the unit suite N times with file concurrency varied between runs, parses each run's TAP down to individual test names and fails on any test whose outcome changed and is not on the quarantine register; it runs weekly in .github/workflows/flake-watch.yml and publishes a dated trail issue, and the register's shape plus its ceiling block on every build.

Already covered: .github/workflows/llm-drift.yml walks the WHOLE registry against the configured provider every Wednesday and publishes a dated pass/fail trail issue, so the item's premise (drift surfaces only when someone runs `npm run test:llm` by hand) is stale; the residual behaviour half (`npm run llm:quality`) cannot be scheduled because its judge is the Claude CLI on the maintainer's subscription, not a runner.

Needs deployment credentials and network: a per-PR preview environment requires a Vercel token this worktree does not carry; the key-free Playwright lane already exercises the running app on every push and PR, so the real residual is that .husky/pre-push runs check:ci without test:e2e, and adding a ~6-minute stage to the operator's push is their cost decision, not mine.

Needs a runtime: there are 88 route handlers under src/app/api, and a contract for them has to be DERIVED and then verified against the source by a gate — hand-authoring 88 request/response schemas with no node, no typecheck and no test runner would produce a document nothing has checked, which is worse than the implementations it replaces.

lessons: This repository already keys its guardrails two ways — .github/contract-ledger.json by the ENFORCEMENT and .github/constraint-map.json by the RULE — and both are held to the tree by unit tests that fail on a claimed-but-absent fence. Adding a guardrail here means adding a row to both plus the AGENTS.md table in the same order; extending an existing mechanism is far cheaper and more honest than inventing a parallel one, and several rows carry a `verdict` field that already names the fence somebody meant to build.

Its exception-ceiling idea (an entry and the ceiling that pays for it in the same diff) generalises cleanly to any number that decides what red means — ratchet baselines, quality floors, LOC limits — which was the largest unfenced surface left: those are one digit inside the gate script itself, so editing one turns a gate green without a build ever going red.

An offline lane can safely extend gate/registry tooling here because the meta-tests (constraint-map, gate-remedy, gate-bite, fence-census) state their invariants explicitly enough to satisfy by reading; what an offline lane cannot do is anything that needs a value from the network (action SHAs, provider answers) or an artefact only a runtime can generate (an API contract, a lockfile, a baseline).
